country.name: Malta
country.tagline: Tiny limestone islands with two native grapes, Ġellewża and Girgentina, and two island appellations.

stats.note: Approximate; Malta has a few hundred hectares of vines and small production (about 630 tonnes of wine in 2005 per Wikipedia). Not reported separately by OIV.

country.overview:
Malta's wine history is Phoenician, Roman and then, for a long time, imported. The modern industry dates from the early twentieth century, when Emmanuel Delicata (1907) and Marsovin (1919) were founded near Paola, but for decades they relied on imported grapes and must. Accession to the EU in 2004 removed protective levies and pushed the islands towards quality: international varieties were planted from the 1970s and especially the 1990s, and estates such as Meridiana (1987), Montekristo, Ta' Betta and Ta' Mena on Gozo now bottle wines from local vineyards.

The point of interest is the two native grapes. Ġellewża is a light, red-fruited black grape often made as rosé or frizzante; Girgentina is a delicate, low-alcohol white. Both are found almost nowhere else. Malta and Gozo each have a PDO (DOK, Denominazzjoni ta' Oriġini Kontrollata), and the Maltese Islands IĠT covers the whole archipelago. Vineyards are small, terraced and walled against the wind, on thin soils over globigerina and coralline limestone, and the hot, dry, windy summers make irrigation and early harvests common.

history.title: Phoenician vines
history.text: Phoenician traders settled Malta and are thought to have introduced the vine; Roman villas such as the one at Rabat later had wine presses.

history.title: Delicata and Marsovin
history.text: Emmanuel Delicata (1907) and Marsovin (1919), both based near Paola, founded Malta's commercial wine industry.

history.title: EU membership and the DOK system
history.text: After accession in 2004 Malta adopted EU wine rules; the PDOs Malta and Gozo were registered in 2009.

country.classification: Two PDOs (DOK Malta and DOK Gozo/Għawdex) and one PGI (IĠT Maltese Islands). DOK wines must come from registered local vineyards with lower yields than IĠT.
country.climate_soils: Hot, dry summers, mild winters, strong winds; thin terra rossa and carbonate soils over globigerina and coralline limestone.

grapes.name: Ġellewża
grapes.note: Native red, light and fruity, often made as rosé or sparkling.

grapes.name: Girgentina
grapes.note: Native white, delicate and low in alcohol, sometimes blended with Chardonnay.

grapes.name: Syrah, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Vermentino

sources.title: EU PDO geospatial inventory (Candiago et al. 2022), Maltese PDO records

regions.name: Maltese Islands
regions.tagline: Walled limestone terraces and two native grapes.
regions.summary: Malta and Gozo each have a PDO; the IĠT Maltese Islands covers both. Vineyards are tiny and scattered among stone walls.
regions.history: Phoenician and Roman winemaking, a twentieth-century industry built on imported grapes, and a quality turn after 2004.
regions.terroir: Globigerina and coralline limestone, thin soils, wind and drought.
regions.classification: DOK Malta, DOK Gozo, IĠT Maltese Islands.

sources.title: EU PDO geospatial inventory (Candiago et al. 2022), Maltese PDO records

mt-gozo.name: Gozo
mt-gozo.grapes: Ġellewża, Girgentina and authorised international varieties
mt-gozo.summary: The PDO for the smaller island of Gozo, greener and more rural than Malta, with small family estates such as Ta' Mena and Tal-Massar around Xagħra and Għarb, near the Neolithic temples of Ġgantija.

mt-malta.name: Malta
mt-malta.grapes: Ġellewża, Girgentina and authorised international varieties
mt-malta.summary: The PDO for wine from vineyards on the main island of Malta, from terraced plots on limestone in the west and north (around Rabat, Mġarr and Siġġiewi). Delicata, Marsovin, Meridiana and Montekristo are the main producers; reds from Syrah and Merlot and whites from Chardonnay and Girgentina dominate.

sites.name: Marsovin Winery
sites.text: Founded in 1919 by the Cassar family at Paola; makes the traditional-method sparkling Cassar de Malte and estate wines from its own vineyards.

sites.name: Emmanuel Delicata Winery
sites.text: Malta's oldest wine company, founded in 1907, on the harbour at Paola; works with contracted growers across both islands.

sites.name: Ta' Mena Estate
sites.text: A family farm and winery near Xagħra on Gozo making DOK Gozo wines alongside olive oil and cheese.

sites.name: Meridiana Wine Estate
sites.text: Founded in 1987 at Ta' Qali, near Mdina, with advice from Antinori; one of the first estates to bottle Maltese-grown international varieties.
